If I could change one thing about iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, I would cancel the new top-to-bottom swipe gesture used to summon Siri AI. Actually, there are already enough ways to invoke Siri, and I've always been used to swiping down from the top to open the Notification Center, so this new gesture doesn't really have much impact on my usage habits.

Speaking of Mac, macOS 27 Golden Gate is almost entirely good news. Although it's already the end of August, new beta versions are still adding many pleasing changes. However, before macOS 27 officially launches next month, there's one more change I'd like to see.

macOS 27 Golden Gate makes it harder to see battery percentage on MacBook

macOS 27 Golden Gate has redesigned the battery control in the menu bar. By default, it only shows the battery icon, not the percentage.

At first glance, this doesn't seem to be a big deal — I've also turned off percentage display on my iPhone myself, as iPhone uses a similar battery icon. However, I've always liked being able to see the battery percentage on Mac.

If you turn on the 'Show Percentage' option in macOS 27 Golden Gate, that number will be placed inside the battery icon. I guess Apple wants to maintain design consistency with iPhones running iOS 27.

Putting the percentage inside the battery icon on iPhone is actually a compromise Apple made to accommodate the limited space on the right side of the 'M-shaped notch' or 'Dynamic Island'. But on Mac, even on the menu bar, I've never experienced a shortage of screen space.

Since the first developer beta, I've been running macOS 27 Golden Gate on a 15-inch MacBook Air. I've found that because it's not that easy to see clearly, I've generally reduced how often I check the battery percentage.

I hope Apple can revisit this point in future design decisions, especially as more and more users find this design problematic. Until then, I've at least found a workaround myself.

I used Codex to write a simple menu bar utility that clearly displays battery status and percentage to suit my own needs. If you find it useful, you can download and install it for free here.
